newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Russian soldier gunned down in Tajik capital.
newsitem.headline: Russian soldier gunned down in Tajik capital.

text.p: One of two Russian soldiers wounded in an attack by unidentified gunmen in the Tajik capital on Wednesday evening has died of his wounds, a Russian military official said on Thursday.

"The servicemen were attacked by unknown criminals who used their usual technique -- shooting from a pistol in the back of the head," Captain Artur Gulko, a Russian military press official, told Reuters. "We qualify this as another act of terrorism."
Gulko said the surviving soldier was in a serious condition. Dozens of Russian servicemen have been killed and wounded in similar attacks in recent months.

No one has claimed responsibility for the killings but they have been blamed widely on armed Islamist opposition fighters struggling against the former Soviet republic's secular government in a bloody four-year civil war.
A ceasefire agreed at the end of last year between the fighters and Tajik government troops appears to be holding.

About 20,000 Russian soldiers carry out peacekeeping duties in Tajikistan and guard its remote, mountainous frontier with Afghanistan. They see themselves as a bulwark against militant Islam on Russia's vulnerable southern flank after the loss of territory which followed the Soviet Union's collapse in 1991.
